faq.a: Evaporation is when a liquid turns into a gas at its surface, below its boiling point. The fastest molecules escape into the air as vapour.

faq.q: Why does evaporation cool things down?
faq.a: The molecules that escape are the most energetic ones, so they carry energy away. What is left behind has less energy, which means it is cooler.

faq.q: Why is it harder to cool down when the air is humid?
faq.a: Humid air already holds lots of water vapour, so sweat evaporates slowly. Without evaporation, sweat just drips and gives little cooling.
asks: Why does humidity make me feel hot?

faq.q: Why does a fan feel cooling?
faq.a: A fan does not cool the air. It blows away the damp air next to your skin and replaces it with drier air, so sweat evaporates faster.
asks: How does a fan cool you?

faq.q: Why do you feel cold getting out of a swimming pool?
faq.a: The water on your skin starts to evaporate and takes heat from your body, especially in a breeze. Drying off with a towel stops it.
asks: Why do I shiver after swimming?

facts: Evaporating one gram of sweat from the skin takes about 2,400 joules of heat from the body.
A person working hard in hot weather can sweat more than a litre an hour.

quiz.say: Why does sweat cool you less on a very humid day?
quiz.show: Why does sweat cool you less on a very humid day?
quiz.why: Cooling comes from sweat evaporating; air already full of vapour slows evaporation, so less heat is carried away.

wrong.0: You still sweat, often more, but the sweat does not evaporate well.
wrong.2: Humid air can be cool or hot; the problem is that it slows evaporation.
